cards.text: We're at the end of Ecclesiastes, and the book steps back to talk about the Teacher, the son of David and king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1). It's like the little "about the author" blurb on the back of a cookbook, and the first thing it says is that he was wise.

cards.question: The Teacher was wise, but he kept all that wisdom to himself.

cards.text: And this man put in the WORK: he pondered, searched out and arranged many proverbs, so he didn't just toss his sayings in a junk drawer and hope for the best. Believe me, friend, I KNOW how that turns out.

cards.question: When the Teacher went searching, what was he looking for?

answers.text: Delightful sayings and accurate words of truth
Secret sayings meant only for the wise
Clever riddles to puzzle the kings

cards.text: Next, the book paints two pictures of what wise words are like. One comes from the field, and one comes from the workshop.

cards.question: The words of the wise are like goads. What does that picture say wise words do to people?

answers.text: They prod people to keep moving
They lull people into a deep rest
They keep people from asking questions

cards.question: The anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails. What does that picture say about those collected sayings?

answers.text: They hold firm and stay put
They bend with every new idea

cards.text: And who's swinging the hammer on those firmly embedded nails? A single Shepherd.
Then the book speaks to “my son” and gives him one more warning. This one's about books and study.

cards.question: The warning to “my son” says the making of many books will soon come to an end.
The warning goes on: much study ___ the body.

cards.text: Now, when all has been heard, here comes the conclusion of the matter. Twelve chapters of searching, and the bottom line is this: fear God and keep His commandments.

cards.question: Why should a person fear God and keep His commandments?

answers.text: Because this is the whole duty of man
Because it wins the praise of others
Because the kings of Israel require it

cards.text: And the very last line of the whole book gives one more reason. God will bring every deed into judgment.

cards.question: God will bring every deed into judgment, but anything done in secret is left out.
God brings every hidden thing into judgment too. Which hidden things does that cover?

findings.problem: Only two cards try for a laugh: the cookbook blurb on card 1 and the junk drawer on card 3. Cards 5, 8, 9, 12 and 14 are plain narration with no reactions, disbelief or self-deprecation. Even the book's big conclusion on card 12 lands flat. Apart from one 'WORK' and one 'KNOW' on card 3, there are no loud moments.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 5 of the 9 choice cards, and fill in the blank appears only once. One type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It names two things and the wrong answers name one, so it is noticeably longer. It also uses the verse's exact phrasing ('delightful sayings,' 'accurate words of truth'), so it sounds more like the Bible than the others. The wording is also slightly off: the text says he searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth. It does not say he was looking for both.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question itself says the nails are 'firmly embedded.' That rules out both wrong answers ('They bend with every new idea' and 'They work loose over time') and repeats the right answer ('They hold firm').

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Twelve chapters of searching' describes the whole book as the Teacher's search. That claim comes from outside this passage, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question says 'every hidden thing,' which rules out 'Only the evil ones' and 'Only the good ones' before the baker picks. The right answer ('Whether good or evil') is also the verse's exact phrase and has a different form from the two 'Only…' answers, so it stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
